scope: SM103 compile-only evidence for Triton Blackwell automatic warp specialization; no runtime or performance claims

github_discussion_audit.purpose: Broad discovery index complementing the curated per-source entries below. It records current-mechanism provenance, maturity/open work, historical routes, and explicit exclusions.
github_discussion_audit.coverage_claim: Systematic, cutoff-bounded audit of searchable issue/PR bodies, comments/reviews, local git history, and blame provenance; not a mathematical enumeration of deleted, edited, unindexed, branch-only, Slack, or internal discussions.

sources.title: Is it possible for Triton to automatically generate warp-specialized FlashAttention-3 style kernels?
distilled_claims: The motivating problem was whether compiler scheduling could overlap TMA, tensor-core work, and attention-side computation without requiring a hand-written role split.
The discussion records the transition from extending software pipelining toward explicit computation partitions and automatic warp specialization.

sources.title: Implement ttg.warp_specialize op
distilled_claims: The TTGIR operation models a default region and asynchronously executed worker partition regions with independent warp counts.
The current IR keeps worker regions in an isolated partitions container and returns values only through the default region.

sources.title: Codegen for ttg.warp_specialize
distilled_claims: Lowering materializes a warp-id dispatch that separates default warps from worker warps and repeatedly dispatches worker partitions.
Warp-group barriers and partition state are part of the generated control protocol, not merely scheduling annotations.

sources.title: Add basic loop partition infra and an SSA dependency rewrite pass
distilled_claims: AutomaticWS began as a dataflow transformation: operations receive partition assignments and cross-partition SSA dependencies require an explicit communication representation.

The current implementation splits proof obligations: partition metadata verification checks attribute locality/well-formedness, PartitionLoops rejects unresolved direct cross-partition SSA, and InsertAref supplies the positive communication rewrite.

sources.title: Implement loop partitioning pass into ttg.warp_specialize
distilled_claims: PartitionLoops turns partition attributes into real default and worker regions only after communication dependencies have been made explicit.
Loop-carried values, captures, and outputs need distinct handling when structured control flow is cloned into partition regions.

sources.title: Automatic warp specialization for simple matmul loops
distilled_claims: The initial Blackwell AutomaticWS path recognized a descriptor-load-to-MMAv5 loop and separated memory and MMA work into asynchronous partitions.
This establishes the canonical positive case but does not imply that every loop carrying warp_specialize intent is eligible.

sources.title: Support persistent matmul in warp specialization
distilled_claims: Persistent matmul extends the positive case from a single K loop to a scheduler-controlled outer tile loop with loop-carried state.
It is an important bridge between simple matmul and later nested attention/grouped-GEMM support.

sources.title: Add an Nvidia Warp Specialization Dialect with an Async Reference Type and Operations
distilled_claims: ARef introduces an IR-level producer-consumer reference whose put/get protocol can later lower to storage plus synchronization.
This decouples partition analysis from immediate commitment to raw shared-memory and barrier instructions.

sources.title: Add a separate pass for optimizing partition num warps
distilled_claims: Logical partition warp counts are optimized after partition materialization, with tensor-layout rewriting used to preserve semantics.
TMEM operations impose a four-warp floor even when an MMA-issuer partition can otherwise be reduced further.

sources.title: Disable integer range analysis
distilled_claims: Integer-range optimization was removed from the AutomaticWS composite pipeline because the upstream pass was not reliable.
The fallback retains SCCP and CSE; this is an optimization-cleanup limitation, not a semantic disablement of warp specialization.

sources.title: Revert enabling createIntRangeOptimizationsPass
distilled_claims: A short-lived attempt to re-enable integer-range optimization was reverted because the pass was still buggy.
The frozen source deliberately leaves the pass commented out and documents the intent to revisit it after an upstream fix.

sources.title: Control dynamic register allocation from Triton
distilled_claims: Partition register requests are compiler estimates used to drive dynamic register reallocation; they are not exact register proofs at TTGIR level.
The IR carries requested and actual register budgets into later warp-group allocation and LLVM lowering.

sources.title: Improve how dynamic register reallocation is implemented
distilled_claims: All warp-specialized sites are padded to a program-wide maximum number of physical warp groups so inactive warps are present to surrender registers.
Register budgets are changed at default/worker partition boundaries, making register ownership a temporal protocol rather than a static partition.

sources.title: Merge warp specialization and pipeliner scheduling
distilled_claims: Loop stage/cluster decisions are established before AutomaticWS, consumed while forming communication, and each resulting loop is scheduled again afterward.
Warp specialization and software pipelining are cooperating transformations rather than alternatives.

sources.title: Don't pipeline loops where latency ops are in the same stage
distilled_claims: After loop partitioning, a role may retain backward-slice operations in several inherited stages even though all of its actual latency operations occupy one stage.
Pipelining that role introduces no overlap and can regress register pressure and instruction scheduling, so its schedule should normalize to one stage.

sources.title: Don't pipeline loops where latency ops are in the same stage (reland)
distilled_claims: The single-stage normalization was relanded with a correction that preserves stages of loads which are genuinely scheduled.
The frozen implementation applies the rule only after projecting an existing WS schedule and inspecting scheduled latency operations.

sources.title: Fix WAR async+generic proxy for warp specialization
distilled_claims: Splitting one loop across partitions can create a new async/generic proxy ordering obligation even when the unspecialized loop was ordered correctly.
Barrier completion and proxy visibility are separate correctness dimensions.

sources.title: Improved partition scheduling pass
distilled_claims: The current scheduler builds a hierarchical dataflow graph, creates initial data partitions, repeatedly merges them using ordered heuristics and constraints, then propagates assignments to supporting operations.
Maintainer review frames AutomaticWS as a loop-local optimization and the partitioner as a heuristic scheduler, not a globally optimal task solver.

sources.title: Reimplement PartitionLoops pass supporting general control flow
distilled_claims: Partition materialization recursively clones structured control flow and remaps operands/results separately for each partition.
Support for general control-flow shape is distinct from the scheduler deciding that a particular loop is eligible and profitable.

sources.title: Update aref ops and lower_aref pass
distilled_claims: ARef indexing is threaded through control flow and determines both the selected buffer stage and mbarrier phase.
LowerAref converts logical channel events into buffer allocation, wait, arrive, and asynchronous-operation tracking.

sources.title: Update RewritePartitionDependencies to insert arefs
distilled_claims: Cross-partition produced values are rewritten into ARef put/get events before code partitioning.
Barrier-backed storage must be invalidated before the same shared-memory bytes are reused for a later barrier lifetime.

sources.title: Make warp specialization require at least 4 warps
distilled_claims: The dialect requires the base warp count of a warp-specialized kernel to be a multiple of four instead of letting downstream warp-group allocation fail.
This is an explicit supported-subset boundary of the current IR and allocator.

sources.title: Add support for WarpSpecialization in ConSan
distilled_claims: Concurrency instrumentation must understand partition execution scopes, captures, asynchronous completion, and shared/TMEM accesses introduced by warp specialization.
Sanitizer support is independent evidence that the implementation treats synchronization as a verifiable semantic contract.

sources.title: Work around race by asserting MMA sync if scales are TMEM allocated before
distilled_claims: Scaled MMA adds scale-operand dependencies that may not be safely pipelineable with the MMA partition.
When the required ordering cannot be represented, the implementation conservatively forces synchronous MMA behavior rather than preserving an unsafe overlap.

sources.title: Enable end-to-end ARef
distilled_claims: ARef insertion and lowering became the active end-to-end communication path inside AutomaticWS rather than a detached experimental dialect.
The current pass pipeline places ARef creation before PartitionLoops and lowers the channel before physical warp-group materialization.

sources.title: Recognize warp-specialized nested loops in AssignLatencies
distilled_claims: Persistent attention can place the warp-specialize marker on an outer scheduler loop while the inner reduction loop is the one processed by the software pipeliner.
WS-specific MMA latency logic must therefore walk enclosing scf.for operations rather than inspect only the current loop.

sources.title: Nested loop support
distilled_claims: Partition propagation and ARef/TMEM handling recurse through nested loops.
TMEM allocation or zero initialization is hoisted only when control-flow analysis can prove the relevant loop executes; otherwise the initialization remains in place.

sources.title: Correctly assign stage and cluster annotation to ARef ops for a block-arg producer
distilled_claims: For a cross-partition value represented by a loop block argument, scheduling must trace through the yield edge to the actual defining operation.
Attention reductions provide a concrete case where treating the block argument itself as the producer loses required stage/cluster information.

sources.title: Store asyncOp per partition
distilled_claims: TMEM producer/consumer bookkeeping must retain an asynchronous operation per partition; a single shared record can alias distinct MMAv5/TMEM dependencies.
A front-end warp-specialize attribute does not prove that partitions were materialized; a loop without an eligible TMA or TCGen5 root may remain unspecialized.

sources.title: Fix AutomaticWS when mixing TMA and non-TMA loads
distilled_claims: When only part of an MMA operand chain moves into a specialized partition, loop scheduling needs self-latency information to insert the required wait.
Mixed descriptor and ordinary loads are supported through explicit conservative scheduling rather than by assuming every operand is asynchronously produced.

sources.title: Filter ARef.get results not produced and last-used in the scheduled loop
distilled_claims: ARef get/channel creation still covers produced values whose defining or consuming scope extends outside the scheduled loop.

Only produced results defined inside the scheduled loop are passed to enter/exit stage-cluster derivation; this avoids assigning that loop's schedule metadata to outside results without turning them into an unsupported communication case.

sources.title: Skip InsertTmemAref if function does not use warp specialization
distilled_claims: The landed guard skips TMEM-ARef insertion when the function has no tt.warp_specialize loop marker, avoiding unrelated TMEM assumptions.

Maintainer review identifies a broader maturity requirement beyond that narrow guard: unsupported invariants should disable the transformation before mutation instead of ending in downstream assertions.

sources.title: Make cluster barriers be executed by all threads
distilled_claims: A cluster barrier cannot be placed in a worker partition that is executed by only a subset of CTA threads; it must be moved to an all-thread control point.
Operations whose lowering requires a cluster-wide rendezvous cannot be arbitrarily isolated in one partition.

sources.title: Concurrency Sanitizer support for detecting incorrect barrier re-initialization
distilled_claims: Reinitializing an mbarrier before invalidating or completing its previous lifetime is a detectable correctness error.
This directly validates the lifecycle assumptions relied on by ARef lowering and shared-memory reuse.

sources.title: Add eligibility checks for memory operations in partition scheduling
distilled_claims: Current Blackwell AutomaticWS requires at least one eligible descriptor memory operation before partition attributes are serialized.
Ordinary pointer loads are not descriptor load/store roots in the current partition classifier, so intent alone does not materialize specialization.

sources.title: Limit warp specialization partition attributes to the WS pass
distilled_claims: Partition annotations are internal scheduling state: selected transformations from PartitionScheduling through LowerAref are each followed by verification; PartitionLoops, LowerWarpGroup, and ScheduleLoops are not wrapped by that verifier, and the attributes are cleared when AutomaticWS finishes materialization.
This prevents stale analysis metadata from leaking into later compiler phases.

sources.title: Fix scaled MMA partition scheduling dependency
distilled_claims: The scaled-MMA token is a real dataflow seed and must participate in partition propagation like the ordinary MMA result.
Otherwise the token-consuming TMEM load and partition output metadata can be disconnected from the producing partition.

sources.title: Fix deadlock detection in WS code
distilled_claims: A static WS participant mask is insufficient because one partition may finish before the others, especially in CLC-controlled code.
ConSan tracks a per-CTA runtime live mask, retires roles at warp_yield or warp_return, and clears the mask at kernel exit.
limitations: Focused FileCheck directly covers active-mask setup and waits; role-retirement and kernel-exit clear hooks are established by frozen source plus PR discussion, but no direct CHECK of those hook calls was found.

sources.title: Implement fence-async-proxy modeling in ConSan
distilled_claims: ConSan records accessed and fenced frontier state per buffer/source and propagates it through barriers so async-proxy legality can be checked across WS partitions.
The model deliberately requires a fence for generic-to-async transitions even for read/read and relies on completion-wait checks for the reverse direction.

sources.title: Scope ConSan cluster visibility to warp partitions
distilled_claims: A cluster barrier inside WS synchronizes matching logical partitions across CTAs, not every partition in the kernel.
Visibility and proxy frontiers must be published only to participant peers; broadcasting all partition columns can hide missing local hand-offs.

sources.title: Allocate warp-specialization mbarriers for atomic ordering
distilled_claims: Multi-CTA atomic_poll and selected atomic acquire/release cases inside a warp-specialized region need cluster-ordering barriers and therefore receive the same per-region double-slot mbarrier allocation as explicit cluster barriers.
Barrier allocation depends on operation semantics and later atomic-ordering lowering, not only on explicit ARef channels or explicit ClusterBarrierOp instances.

sources.title: Fix use-list iterator invalidation in cloneMultiPartitionDataOps
distilled_claims: Cloning data operations for several partitions mutates SSA use lists, so traversal must be stable under rewrite.
This recent hardening fix is evidence that canonical paths are actively maintained while unusual small-tile attention shapes can still expose compiler robustness bugs.

sources.title: CUDA Programming Guide: Compute Capabilities and feature-set compiler targets
distilled_claims: Compute capability 10.3 belongs to the compute_100f feature family, while compute_103f names the 10.3 family target and architecture-specific features require the corresponding architecture target.
The article must record the exact feature-set target used for compile-only evidence instead of treating every major-version-10 target as identical.

sources.title: PTX ISA: Tensor Memory and Fifth-Generation TensorCore instructions
distilled_claims: TCGen05 MMA accumulators reside in TMEM; MMA issue, TMEM allocation, and TMEM register load/store have different thread/warp issue granularities.

MMA completion tracking uses tcgen05.commit with an mbarrier. In the canonical MMA-to-TMEM-load sequence, commit implicitly supplies the before-thread-sync side, so no explicit before fence or CTA barrier is required; PTX separately requires tcgen05.fence::after_thread_sync before the asynchronous tcgen05.ld, followed by tcgen05.wait::ld before consuming its register results.

The frozen Triton dialect/lowering/tests and the exact SM103 artifact contain commit, mbarrier wait, tcgen05.ld, and wait::ld but omit the specialized after-thread-sync fence. Assembly success therefore does not qualify this cross-thread ordering contract or runtime correctness.

sources.title: PTX ISA: mbarrier, named barriers, asynchronous completion, and proxy fences
distilled_claims: An mbarrier phase completes only after its pending arrival count and asynchronous transaction count are satisfied; phase/parity is part of the hardware protocol.
CTA named barriers coordinate participating threads, whereas proxy fences order visibility between memory proxies; neither substitutes for the other.

sources.title: PTX ISA: setmaxnreg dynamic register allocation
distilled_claims: setmaxnreg.inc/dec transfers per-thread register capacity through a CTA register pool, and all warps in a physical warpgroup must execute a consistent instruction.
Requested values are constrained to the ISA range and granularity, and synchronization is required around successive ownership changes.

sources.title: CUDA Programming Guide: Tensor Memory Accelerator and producer-consumer warp specialization
distilled_claims: A global-to-shared TMA operation can be issued by one elected thread and reports completion through an mbarrier tracking expected bytes.
Assigning TMA issue to a specialized low-register partition is a compiler scheduling choice for overlap and lifetime control, not a requirement that the hardware reserve a complete producer warp.

sources.title: NVIDIA Blackwell Tuning Guide
distilled_claims: Datacenter Blackwell exposes a 64K 32-bit register file per SM and at most 255 registers per thread, which bounds the register budget redistributed by AutomaticWS.
Thread-block clusters and distributed shared memory add scope and resource constraints that the compiler must respect even in compile-only legality analysis.

sources.title: triton.language.range warp_specialize parameter
distilled_claims: The user-facing flag asks the compiler to partition memory, MMA, and vector operations into asynchronous partitions and may increase total warps.

The official API still documents Blackwell simple matmul loops as the supported baseline, so broader current tests should be presented as implementation growth rather than an unrestricted API guarantee.

sources.title: TritonGPUOps: ttg.warp_specialize
distilled_claims: The operation's public IR contract exposes partition warp counts, warp-group start IDs, requested registers, actual registers, explicit captures, and an isolated partitions container.
Worker partitions currently cannot return values directly; the default region carries operation results.

sources.title: Warp Specialization in Triton: Design and Roadmap
distilled_claims: The official design decomposes AutomaticWS into data partitioning, software-pipeline scheduling, partition scheduling, communication-buffer creation, memory planning, channel creation, and code partitioning.

It explicitly describes compiler support as limited and experimental and identifies simple heuristics, generalized kernels, debugging, profile guidance, and richer hardware specialization as ongoing work.
Because the article is a January 2026 snapshot, claims about what has landed are reconciled against the frozen July 2026 source rather than copied as current truth.

sources.title: Tawa: Automatic Warp Specialization for Modern GPUs with Asynchronous References
distilled_claims: Tawa defines an asynchronous reference as a logical producer-consumer channel backed by payload storage and empty/full synchronization state, with put/get/consumed operations and circular multi-buffering.
Its task-aware partitioning motivates following data dependencies from side-effecting roots and duplicating cheap dependency-closed computations where that avoids illegal cross-task SSA edges.
The paper supplies design provenance for ARef, while the frozen Triton implementation remains authoritative for exact pass order and supported cases.
